key_insight: Calibrated XGBoost performed best among the evaluated models for retrospectively identifying a composite of documented suicide-related outcomes in an age-matched EHR cohort.
clinical_relevance: EHR-derived clinical and social-contextual features may support suicide-risk research, but these findings do not establish readiness for clinical screening.
method: Grouped MIMIC-IV diagnosis codes into clinically motivated features and a composite suicide-related outcome.
Retained all positive patients and sampled age-matched comparison patients to address imbalance and age confounding.
Compared logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost with isotonic calibration; used SHAP for feature interpretation.
evidence_signal: In MIMIC-IV evaluations before and after resampling, calibrated XGBoost showed the strongest matched-cohort performance; the abstract reports no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Retrospective coded outcomes and resampled cohorts may not reflect prospective risk or real-world prevalence, requiring external and prospective validation.
paper_title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
